categoryNote: All adapter-level entries are ADAPTER-INSTANCE-PARAMETERIZED: the implementation accepts an adapter alias / interface index and otherwise enumerates eligible adapters at runtime; nothing is hardcoded per vendor or per machine. Every write is capability-probed first (Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty must show the driver exposing the keyword; numeric values are clamped to Ndi\Params min/max/step or the driver's enumerated value list) and only-if-present - NEXTRIX never creates a vendor keyword. Virtual/VPN/WAN adapters (Virtual/HardwareInterface flags plus the research term list) are excluded from tuning, and Wi-Fi (PhysicalMediaType 'Native 802.11') is excluded from every Ethernet-specific entry while the Wi-Fi entries refuse non-Wi-Fi adapters. LSO, Flow Control, checksum offloads and jumbo frames stay ADVANCED + preset-excluded with their trade-offs stated in plain text. Implementation: src/nxcore/functions/NX07.ps1 (NX07-001..022 plus Invoke-Nx07Rollback). No entry contains a latency/FPS/throughput claim; configuration intent only.

tweaks.name: Adapter inventory & capability report
tweaks.description: Read-only inventory of every network adapter with the advanced-property keywords each driver exposes, its power-management surface, and the tuning exclusion decision.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner and the other NX07 entries a driver-capability map before any network change is selected.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Enumerates Get-NetAdapter, classifies each instance by PhysicalMediaType ('802.3' Ethernet, 'Native 802.11' Wi-Fi, 'WirelessWan' WAN), and excludes virtual/VPN/debug adapters through HardwareInterface=false, Virtual=true and the research term list (r4 network.bat / SynToolkit). For every remaining adapter it reports each Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty row (RegistryKeyword, display name, current value, driver ValidRegistryValues/ValidDisplayValues), the Get-NetAdapterPowerManagement properties, the Get-NetAdapterRss queue view, and the resolved NIC class key used for Ndi\Params probing. MAC addresses are masked to the vendor OUI because they are device identifiers. No write, no journal requirement, and no performance verdict: the report answers 'does this driver expose the keyword at all', which is the precondition every other NX07 entry enforces before writing.
tweaks.defaultState: Information only; no NEXTRIX network report exists.
tweaks.proposedState: Machine-readable adapter/capability report (object or JSON file in a chosen folder).

verify.procedure: Report lists every adapter with its media type, exclusion decision, advanced-property count and available RegistryKeywords with the driver's own value lists.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - read-only diagnostic.

originalState.method: Not applicable - read-only.

sideEffects: None (read-only).
documentationSource: r4-synergy-ultraos.md (Ndi\Params probing; virtual-adapter exclusion; PhysicalAdapter filter)

tweaks.name: Adapter power management
tweaks.description: Configures the documented per-adapter power-management features (selective suspend, device sleep on disconnect, wake patterns, D0 coalescing, offloads) for the chosen physical adapter.
tweaks.objective: Let the owner stop adapter-level power transitions on a desktop NIC while keeping the trade-off explicit and reversible.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Per adapter through Get-/Set-NetAdapterPowerManagement (documented cmdlet surface). Each requested property is compared with the live value; properties the driver reports as 'Unsupported' are skipped and reported, never forced, and already-at-state properties produce a journaled skip. The device checkbox 'AllowComputerToTurnOffDevice' is CAPTURED AND REPORTED but intentionally not modified: no documented NetAdapter cmdlet parameter writes it, and NEXTRIX will not substitute an undocumented WMI write to fake support. Trade-off recorded honestly: disabling selective suspend / sleep-on-disconnect can keep the link powered while idle or unplugged (power draw and heat) and some drivers handle these transitions badly - hence CONDITIONAL and never automatic. Values are applied with -NoRestart and take effect at the next adapter restart or reboot; NEXTRIX does not restart adapters by default.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows/driver default power management (commonly selective suspend enabled on Ethernet).
tweaks.proposedState: Requested power-management features disabled (or set) per adapter, with Unsupported properties reported untouched.

verify.procedure: Get-NetAdapterPowerManagement re-read shows every changed property at the requested value; Unsupported properties remain reported as Unsupported; skip entries are journaled for no-op properties.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx07Rollback restores each changed property to its captured original only while the live value still equals the NEXTRIX-recorded value; a property the owner changed afterwards is reported diverged and left untouched.

originalState.method: Full power-management property set captured per adapter (including AllowComputerToTurnOffDevice and RsnRekeyOffload) before any write.

sideEffects: Higher idle power draw / heat when sleep-on-disconnect and selective suspend are disabled.
Driver-conditional behavior: Unsupported features are never forced.
Effective at the next adapter restart/reboot (NEXTRIX does not restart adapters).
documentationSource: r4-synergy-ultraos.md (NIC power keywords: per-adapter, presence-gated, documented costs)

tweaks.name: Energy Efficient Ethernet
tweaks.description: Enables or disables the driver-exposed Energy-Efficient Ethernet keyword on the chosen physical Ethernet adapter.
tweaks.objective: Expose EEE as an opt-in, driver-honest switch rather than a silent vendor default change.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Targets the standardized *EEE keyword (with the non-prefixed 'EEE'/'AdvancedEEE' vendor exposures as fallbacks) on Ethernet adapters only. The keyword is written ONLY if Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty shows it; the requested state is mapped by DISPLAY NAME ('Enabled'/'Disabled') onto the driver's own ValidRegistryValues, never by guessing integer meaning, and a driver whose enumeration cannot express the request is skipped with the value list in the reason. EEE is a vendor implementation with documented link-power behavior, but NEXTRIX makes no claim about any outcome - the entry exists because owners ask to turn it off when a switch/NIC combination misbehaves, and because turning it back ON is an equally valid configuration. ADVANCED and preset-excluded: link-partner compatibility varies. The write uses -NoRestart and takes effect at the next adapter restart/reboot.
tweaks.defaultState: Driver default (varies by vendor and firmware).
tweaks.proposedState: *EEE = Disabled (or Enabled) on the selected Ethernet adapter, journaled and verified.

verify.procedure: Re-read of the same RegistryKeyword returns the requested RegistryValue; a driver that does not expose the keyword yields a PropertyNotExposed skip entry instead of a fabricated keyword.

rollback.procedure: Standard only-if-ours restore of the exact captured RegistryValue for that keyword; changed-elsewhere values are reported diverged.

originalState.method: Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty capture of RegistryValue/DisplayValue plus adapter identity (alias, ifIndex, GUID, PnP id) and NIC class key.

sideEffects: Link-partner dependent behavior; a marginal cable/switch may negotiate differently.
Effective at the next adapter restart/reboot.
documentationSource: r4-synergy-ultraos.md (*EEE set only after Ndi\Params capability probing)

tweaks.name: Interrupt moderation
tweaks.description: Enables or disables the driver-exposed interrupt-moderation keyword on the chosen physical Ethernet adapter.
tweaks.objective: Offer the documented moderation switch with an explicit statement that its trade-off is vendor-defined and unmeasured here.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Targets *InterruptModeration (fallback 'InterruptModeration') on Ethernet adapters only, present-only, with the requested state mapped by display name onto the driver's enumeration. Interrupt moderation is a documented NDIS standardized keyword: it batches receive/transmit completions to reduce per-packet CPU work, and vendors document their own variants and rate keywords. NEXTRIX deliberately does not write vendor rate keywords (they differ wildly) and makes NO measurement claim: the entry records the configuration intent and the owner-visible trade-off (CPU cost versus per-packet handling) without asserting an outcome. ADVANCED and preset-excluded because a bad rate/mode combination on a specific driver is a real support boundary documented in the reference research. The write uses -NoRestart.
tweaks.defaultState: Driver default (commonly Enabled).
tweaks.proposedState: *InterruptModeration = Disabled (or Enabled) on the selected Ethernet adapter.

verify.procedure: Re-read of *InterruptModeration returns the requested value, or a PropertyNotExposed skip is journaled when the driver lacks the keyword.

rollback.procedure: Only-if-ours restore of the captured original value; divergent values are reported, never overwritten.

originalState.method: Capability + current value capture via Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty, with adapter identity and class key.

sideEffects: Vendor-defined behavior; a specific driver may expose only a rate variant, in which case this entry skips.
Effective at the next adapter restart/reboot.
documentationSource: r4-synergy-ultraos.md (Intel ITR noted; vendor rate keywords deliberately not touched)

tweaks.name: Receive Side Scaling configuration
tweaks.description: Enables or disables RSS and optionally bounds the RSS processor count on the chosen physical Ethernet adapter.
tweaks.objective: Configure the documented RSS keyword and, when a limit is requested, clamp it to the machine's logical processors and the driver's range.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Writes *RSS (fallback 'RSS') present-only, mapped through the driver's display enumeration, and optionally *MaxRssProcessors. The processor count is clamped to the INTERSECTION of the requested value, the installed logical processor count ([Environment]::ProcessorCount) and the driver's Ndi\Params/enumerated range - a queue count larger than the CPU topology is meaningless by construction, so it is never written. The current queue view (NumberOfReceiveQueues/MaxProcessors) is reported from Get-NetAdapterRss when the driver exposes it, and the logical processor count is recorded next to it so the owner can see the ratio. Enabling more queues is not claimed to improve anything: this is a configuration control whose effect is workload- and driver-dependent (E2+ owner evidence required). ADVANCED and preset-excluded. The write uses -NoRestart.
tweaks.defaultState: Driver default (commonly RSS enabled with a vendor queue count).
tweaks.proposedState: *RSS = Enabled/Disabled; optional *MaxRssProcessors clamped to [1, logical processors].

verify.procedure: Re-read of *RSS (and *MaxRssProcessors when requested) matches the requested/clamped values; the RSS queue view and logical processor count are reported.

rollback.procedure: Only-if-ours restore per keyword (each is a separate journal entry); divergence is reported.

originalState.method: Per-keyword capability/value capture plus adapter identity; queue view and CPU count recorded as context, not as a target.

sideEffects: Queue distribution is driver- and topology-dependent; reducing queues can concentrate interrupt work on fewer CPUs (vendor-defined).
Effective at the next adapter restart/reboot.
documentationSource: r4-synergy-ultraos.md (RSS keyword set only after capability probing)

tweaks.name: Receive Segment Coalescing
tweaks.description: Enables or disables the driver-exposed RSC keywords (IPv4 and IPv6) on the chosen physical Ethernet adapter.
tweaks.objective: Configure RSC per family with present-only writes instead of a single guessed keyword.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Writes every exposed keyword from *RscIPv4/*RscIPv6 (fallback non-prefixed forms) as one entry, each journaled separately so rollback is per-family exact. RSC merges received segments before delivery; the feature is vendor-documented, but its interaction with packet-capture/AV filter drivers is a documented support boundary, which is why this stays ADVANCED and preset-excluded. A driver exposing only one family gets only that family written and the absent one reported. No performance claim is made; the entry records configuration intent and the owner-visible trade-off. Writes use -NoRestart.
tweaks.defaultState: Driver default (varies; many desktop drivers ship RSC disabled).
tweaks.proposedState: *RscIPv4/*RscIPv6 = Disabled (or Enabled) where exposed.

verify.procedure: Per-keyword re-read shows the requested value; absent families are reported as skipped with the probed keyword trail.

rollback.procedure: Only-if-ours restore of each family's captured value, independently.

originalState.method: Per-family capability/value capture (adapter identity + keyword + value).

sideEffects: Coalescing can interact with capture/filter drivers (vendor-documented boundary).
Effective at the next adapter restart/reboot.

tweaks.name: Large Send Offload
tweaks.description: Enables or disables LSO v2 (IPv4 and IPv6) on the chosen physical Ethernet adapter, with the community controversy stated honestly.
tweaks.objective: Offer the documented LSO switch without pretending the conflicting community advice has been resolved.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Writes every exposed keyword from *LsoV2IPv4/*LsoV2IPv6 (fallbacks included), each journaled separately. HONEST NOTE: LSO is the canonical 'unknown benefit' item in the reference research - a hardened playbook (r4 UltraOS) explicitly refuses to touch LSO and Flow Control because forcing them can cause dropped frames on some drivers, while other guides disable LSO by habit. NEXTRIX does not resolve that disagreement and makes no claim either way: the entry is a capability-checked, reversible switch for owners who need it, ADVANCED and preset-excluded. A driver exposing neither keyword is skipped, never invented. Writes use -NoRestart.
tweaks.defaultState: Driver default (commonly Enabled).
tweaks.proposedState: LSO v2 per family = Disabled (or Enabled) where exposed.

verify.procedure: Per-keyword re-read matches the request; absent keywords produce a PropertyNotExposed skip with the probe trail.

rollback.procedure: Only-if-ours restore per family; divergence reported.

originalState.method: Per-family capability/value capture with adapter identity.

sideEffects: Documented driver-dependent frame handling; some vendors report dropped frames when offloads are forced (hence preset-excluded and opt-in).
Effective at the next adapter restart/reboot.
documentationSource: r4-synergy-ultraos.md (LSO/FlowControl/offloads listed as 'unknown benefit - do not touch'; Atlas loop bug noted)

tweaks.name: Checksum offloads (TCP/UDP)
tweaks.description: Sets the driver-exposed IPv4/IPv6 IP/TCP/UDP checksum-offload keywords to a chosen four-state mode.
tweaks.objective: Provide the documented offload control with its controversy stated and no claim of benefit.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Writes every exposed keyword from the family *IPChecksumOffloadIPv4, *TCPChecksumOffloadIPv4, *TCPChecksumOffloadIPv6, *UDPChecksumOffloadIPv4, *UDPChecksumOffloadIPv6 (one journal entry per keyword). The requested mode (Disabled / TxEnabled / RxEnabled / TxRxEnabled) is mapped onto each driver's own enumeration by DISPLAY NAME ('Rx & Tx Enabled' etc.), never by assumed integers; a keyword whose enumeration is absent is skipped. HONEST SCOPE: the shipped default proposal is TxRxEnabled, i.e. the documented Windows/driver default - NEXTRIX does not tell owners that disabling checksum offloads is beneficial. Disabling is offered for troubleshooting only, and the entry stays ADVANCED and preset-excluded because some drivers implement offload paths poorly. Writes use -NoRestart.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows/driver default: checksum offloads enabled (Rx & Tx).
tweaks.proposedState: Chosen four-state mode per exposed checksum keyword; the default proposal keeps offloads enabled.

verify.procedure: Every written keyword re-reads to the requested registry value; keywords not exposed are reported skipped.

rollback.procedure: Per-keyword only-if-ours restore of the captured value.

originalState.method: Per-keyword capture of RegistryValue/DisplayValue plus the driver's valid value lists.

sideEffects: Disabling checksum offloads moves checksum work to the CPU (vendor/driver-dependent).
Effective at the next adapter restart/reboot.
documentationSource: r4-synergy-ultraos.md (offload keywords excluded from blind tuning)

tweaks.name: Flow Control
tweaks.description: Sets the driver-exposed Flow Control keyword to a chosen four-state mode, with the switch dependency stated.
tweaks.objective: Expose the documented pause-frame control while making its segment-wide dependency explicit.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Writes *FlowControl (fallback 'FlowControl') present-only, mapping Disabled / TxEnabled / RxEnabled / TxRxEnabled onto the driver's display enumeration. Flow control is a switch/NIC negotiation: pause frames affect the whole segment, so a host-side change can be moot or harmful depending on what the switch advertises. The reference research lists Flow Control among the 'unknown benefit - do not touch' items (r4), so NEXTRIX ships the documented Windows default (TxRxEnabled) as the default proposal and keeps the entry ADVANCED, preset-excluded and opt-in; diagnostic disabling is possible but not recommended in the text. No claim is made in either direction. Writes use -NoRestart.
tweaks.defaultState: Driver/switch negotiated default (commonly Rx & Tx enabled).
tweaks.proposedState: Chosen mode on the selected Ethernet adapter, journaled and verified.

verify.procedure: Re-read of *FlowControl matches the requested registry value; the driver's supported subset is reported (some expose only Disabled / Rx&Tx).

rollback.procedure: Only-if-ours restore of the captured value.

originalState.method: Capability + value capture via Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty with adapter identity.

sideEffects: Switch-dependent: a host-side setting cannot guarantee segment behavior.
Effective at the next adapter restart/reboot.
documentationSource: r4-synergy-ultraos.md (FlowControl in the do-not-touch list; 'could cause dropped network frames')

tweaks.name: Jumbo Frames
tweaks.description: Sets the adapter jumbo-frame keyword to a driver-enumerated payload size, with the end-to-end path requirement documented.
tweaks.objective: Enable jumbo frames only where the driver exposes the exact size, and state that the whole path must agree.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Targets *JumboPacket (fallback 'JumboPacket'); the requested MTU must be ONE OF THE DRIVER'S ENUMERATED VALUES (e.g. 1514/4088/9014) - NEXTRIX never writes an arbitrary size, and a request the driver cannot express is skipped with the driver's value list in the reason. END-TO-END REQUIREMENT: jumbo frames only work when every hop (NIC, switch, router, peer) supports the same or larger MTU; otherwise large packets are dropped or fragmented. NEXTRIX cannot verify remote hops from the host, so this entry is ADVANCED + preset-excluded and its verify step only proves the local configuration. The interface MTU itself is NX07-018's target; if the adapter keyword is enabled above 1500 while the interface MTU is not, NX07-018's return object reports the inconsistency (it does not silently change it). Writes use -NoRestart.
tweaks.defaultState: Disabled (1514) on most desktop drivers.
tweaks.proposedState: *JumboPacket = a driver-enumerated jumbo size (e.g. 9014) on the selected Ethernet adapter.

verify.procedure: Re-read of *JumboPacket equals the enumerated value; the interface MTU is reported separately and a mismatch above 1500 is called out.

rollback.procedure: Only-if-ours restore of the captured value (usually 1514 = Disabled).

originalState.method: Capability capture including the driver's ValidRegistryValues/ValidDisplayValues, so only enumerated sizes can be written.

sideEffects: Any hop without matching MTU support can drop or fragment large frames - a connectivity symptom, not a performance claim.
Effective at the next adapter restart/reboot.
documentationSource: r4-synergy-ultraos.md (jumbo keyword capped to the driver/path; capability-aware writes)

tweaks.name: Receive/Transmit buffer sizing
tweaks.description: Sets the driver-exposed receive/transmit buffer keywords, clamped to the driver's documented range and a sanity window.
tweaks.objective: Allow buffer-depth configuration without writing values the driver does not document.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Targets *ReceiveBuffers and *TransmitBuffers independently (at least one requested). Each numeric value is clamped to the driver's documented range: the enumerated numeric value list when present, otherwise Ndi\Params min/max/step (probed read-only from the adapter's class key), otherwise the NEXTRIX absolute sanity window [32..8192]. Every clamp is reported with the source range, and step alignment is applied so the written value is a legal driver value. Raising buffers makes the adapter reserve more host/driver memory; NEXTRIX makes no claim that a specific depth is better and ships a conservative default proposal. ADVANCED and preset-excluded because buffer exhaustion and driver-specific ceilings are real support boundaries. Writes use -NoRestart.
tweaks.defaultState: Driver default (vendor-specific; commonly 512 receive / 128 transmit on desktop GbE).
tweaks.proposedState: Requested buffer depths clamped to the driver's documented range, journaled with the clamp report.

verify.procedure: Re-read of each written keyword equals the clamped value; the clamp note records requested vs written and the range source.

rollback.procedure: Per-keyword only-if-ours restore of the captured original depth.

originalState.method: Per-keyword capture plus Ndi\Params range probe (min/max/step) recorded for audit.

sideEffects: Larger buffers reserve more driver/host memory; a driver may cap far below the request (reported).
Effective at the next adapter restart/reboot.
documentationSource: r4-synergy-ultraos.md (SynergyOS caps receive/transmit buffers; UltraOS only-if-present rule)

tweaks.name: Wi-Fi roaming aggressiveness
tweaks.description: Sets the driver-exposed Wi-Fi roaming-aggressiveness keyword to a named strength on the chosen Wi-Fi adapter.
tweaks.objective: Expose the roaming preference as a named, driver-validated choice for environments where the default roams too eagerly or too stickily.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Wi-Fi only: the adapter must report PhysicalMediaType 'Native 802.11' (the r1 *PhysicalMediaType 9/16 rule), otherwise the entry refuses. The keyword is resolved from an ordered candidate list that covers both standardized and vendor exposures - *RoamingAggressiveness, RoamingAggressiveness, RoamIndicateTh (observed on a real MediaTek MT7921), RoamingLevel - and the FIRST exposed keyword wins. The requested strength (Lowest..Highest) is matched against the driver's friendly display names after stripping display ordinals like '2. Lowest', because ordinal numbering is presentation order and does not reliably encode level semantics; an enumeration that cannot express the request is skipped with the driver's value list. Environment-dependent by nature: an aggressive value can move the client between APs unnecessarily, a low value can keep a weak association, and NEXTRIX cannot see the RF environment or the AP's steering policy. CONDITIONAL, offered, never automatic. Writes use -NoRestart.
tweaks.defaultState: Driver default (vendor-specific roaming preference).
tweaks.proposedState: Named roaming strength written to the first driver-exposed roaming keyword.

verify.procedure: Re-read of the resolved keyword equals the requested driver value; the keyword probed and the driver's enumeration are recorded in the report.

rollback.procedure: Only-if-ours restore of the captured value on the resolved keyword.

originalState.method: Capability capture of every candidate keyword (present/absent trail) plus the resolved keyword's RegistryValue/DisplayValue and adapter identity.

sideEffects: RF-environment dependent: behavior can change near roaming boundaries; no guarantee either way.
Effective at the next adapter restart/reboot.
documentationSource: r1-fsosx-xos.md (Wi-Fi identification via *PhysicalMediaType before NIC tuning)

tweaks.name: Wi-Fi preferred band
tweaks.description: Sets the driver-exposed preferred-band keyword to a named band preference on the chosen Wi-Fi adapter.
tweaks.objective: Let the owner express a band preference where the driver supports it, with the AP-capability caveat stated.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Wi-Fi only (PhysicalMediaType 'Native 802.11'). Resolves the first exposed keyword from *PreferredBand / PreferredBand / BandSelection and maps NoPreference / Prefer24GHz / Prefer5GHz / Prefer6GHz onto the driver's display enumeration ('No Preference', 'All Band', 'Prefer 2.4GHz band', '5G Only', ...). AP CAPABILITY IS NOT HOST-VERIFIABLE: whether the access point actually offers the preferred band (and whether 6 GHz exists at all) is outside what Get-NetAdapter can report, so NEXTRIX states the condition instead of pretending to check it. A driver without a 6 GHz enumeration simply cannot express Prefer6GHz and the entry skips with the driver's list. CONDITIONAL, offered, never automatic. Writes use -NoRestart.
tweaks.defaultState: Driver default (commonly no preference).
tweaks.proposedState: Named band preference on the resolved keyword.

verify.procedure: Re-read of the resolved keyword matches the requested display/registry value; the driver's available bands are listed in the report.

rollback.procedure: Only-if-ours restore of the captured original preference.

originalState.method: Candidate-keyword capability trail + captured value for the resolved keyword.

sideEffects: If the AP does not serve the preferred band, the client can end up on a weaker alternative or re-scan more often (AP-dependent, owner-visible).
Effective at the next adapter restart/reboot.

tweaks.name: Wi-Fi channel width
tweaks.description: Sets the driver-exposed per-band channel-width keyword to a chosen width, using only widths the driver enumerates.
tweaks.objective: Allow a width preference per band without writing a width the driver cannot express.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Wi-Fi only. The band selects the keyword candidate set: 2.4 GHz tries *ChannelWidth24, BWSelection24G (observed on MediaTek), then *ChannelWidth/ChannelWidth; 5 GHz tries *ChannelWidth52, BWSelection5G, then the generic pair. The requested width (Auto/20/40/80/160) is matched against the driver's display enumeration ('Auto', '20MHz only', ...), and an inexpressible width is skipped with the driver's list. AP-DEPENDENT AND INTERFERENCE-DEPENDENT: the AP decides the operating width; a host preference can only bias it, and wider channels share spectrum with neighbors (narrower settings are a common mitigation in dense environments). For that reason the entry is ADVANCED + preset-excluded and makes no claim about which width is better. Writes use -NoRestart.
tweaks.defaultState: Driver default (commonly Auto).
tweaks.proposedState: Chosen width on the resolved per-band keyword.

verify.procedure: Re-read of the resolved keyword equals the requested value; the driver's supported widths are reported when the request is refused.

rollback.procedure: Only-if-ours restore of the captured width.

originalState.method: Per-band candidate probing trail plus the resolved keyword's captured value.

sideEffects: AP- and interference-dependent; a width the AP cannot use may be silently ignored by the driver.
Effective at the next adapter restart/reboot.

tweaks.name: Wi-Fi transmit power
tweaks.description: Sets the driver-exposed transmit-power keyword to a named strength on the chosen Wi-Fi adapter.
tweaks.objective: Expose the transmit-power preference where the driver documents named levels, with regulatory limits acknowledged.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Wi-Fi only. Resolves the first exposed keyword from *TransmitPower / TxPowerLevel (observed on MediaTek) / TransmitPowerLevel / TransmitPower, then maps Lowest/Low/Medium/High/Highest by DISPLAY NAME ('1. Highest', '2. Lowest', ...). Name mapping is deliberate: some drivers number their levels in the opposite direction from the strength, so an integer guess would invert the request. Regulatory and driver ceilings always win - the written value is only what the driver enumerates. Reducing power is a legitimate configuration for coverage shaping; increasing it cannot exceed the regulatory/driver cap and NEXTRIX makes no range or outcome claim. CONDITIONAL, offered, never automatic. Writes use -NoRestart.
tweaks.defaultState: Driver default (commonly the highest permitted level).
tweaks.proposedState: Named strength on the resolved transmit-power keyword.

verify.procedure: Re-read of the resolved keyword matches the requested display value; the driver's level list is reported.

rollback.procedure: Only-if-ours restore of the captured level.

originalState.method: Candidate probing trail + captured value/display for the resolved keyword.

sideEffects: Regulatory/driver caps apply; lower power can reduce usable range (owner-visible).
Effective at the next adapter restart/reboot.
documentationSource: r4-synergy-ultraos.md (vendor keyword probing; no blind integer writes)

tweaks.name: DNS configuration
tweaks.description: Configures per-interface DNS servers with a mandatory resolve-probe verification and automatic rollback on failure; optional DoH registration through documented cmdlets.
tweaks.objective: Change resolver choice safely: capture exactly, write, prove the new resolvers answer, and put the original back automatically if they do not.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Per interface: Get-DnsClientServerAddress captures IPv4 and IPv6 server lists plus each family's DHCP provenance (Get-NetIPInterface Dhcp), then Set-DnsClientServerAddress writes the requested list. The cmdlet has NO address-family switch - one call sets the interface's complete server list - so IPv4 and IPv6 are combined and an untouched family is carried over explicitly (recorded in the journal). VERIFY-AND-AUTO-ROLLBACK IS MANDATORY (r5 Sophia pattern): after the write, Resolve-DnsName resolves a stable probe name THROUGH each new server with two attempts per server; one answering resolver is sufficient. If no configured resolver answers, the captured original is restored immediately (ResetServerAddresses when the original was DHCP-provided, otherwise the exact captured list) and the attempt is journaled Failed-RestoredOriginal. DoH is optional and uses only the documented DnsClient cmdlets (Get-/Add-/Remove-DnsClientDohServerAddress) with AutoUpgrade and UDP fallback; an existing registration is never modified, and rollback removes only registrations NEXTRIX added. NO LATENCY OR THROUGHPUT CLAIM is made anywhere: the motivation is resolver choice and optional encrypted transport, and the probe proves reachability only. Invalid addresses, wrong-family entries and more than three servers per family are refused before any capture.
tweaks.defaultState: DNS servers as provided by DHCP/RA or previously configured manually.
tweaks.proposedState: Requested resolver list on the selected interface(s), verified by a live resolve probe, with optional DoH registration.

verify.procedure: Re-read proves the interface's server lists equal the requested ones AND Resolve-DnsName answered through at least one new server. A failed probe triggers immediate auto-rollback and a Failed-RestoredOriginal journal record.

rollback.procedure: Only-if-ours: the live lists must still equal the NEXTRIX-recorded lists; then the captured original is restored (exact list, or automatic configuration when both families were DHCP). DoH registrations added by NEXTRIX are removed; pre-existing ones are untouched.

originalState.method: Per-interface IPv4/IPv6 server lists + DHCP Enabled/Disabled provenance + interface GUID/alias captured before the write; DoH pre-existence checked per server before registration.

sideEffects: A non-answering resolver is rolled back automatically; a resolver that answers but filters content is not detectable by the probe.
DoH availability depends on the resolver; UDP fallback is enabled so name resolution still works if DoH fails.
No improvement in any network timing metric is claimed or measured.

tweaks.name: TCP auto-tuning & ECN inspection/config
tweaks.description: Inspects the machine's TCP global parameters from documented netsh output and, on request, sets auto-tuning level and ECN capability with raw prior values journaled.
tweaks.objective: Make TCP global state visible first, and change it only deliberately with the exact prior text recoverable.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Reads `netsh int tcp show global` (documented) and parses the English labels for Receive Window Auto-Tuning Level, ECN Capability, RSS/RSC state, congestion provider, RFC 1323 timestamps and Initial RTO. With no parameters the function is INSPECTION ONLY: it journals a ReportOnly skip entry (targetType tcpGlobalReport) and returns the parsed fields - no mutation, no journal requirement beyond an existing journal directory. With -AutoTuningLevel and/or -Ecn it captures the RAW prior output plus the parsed fields, runs `netsh int tcp set global`, re-reads and compares, and on a verification failure attempts to write the captured prior values back. The default proposal is the documented Windows client default (normal auto-tuning, ECN disabled), so applying it is expected to be a journaled AlreadyAtState skip - the entry exists so an owner can SEE the state and, when a documented symptom calls for it, change one field with a recoverable prior value. ADVANCED and preset-excluded. No claim is made about any TCP parameter's effect.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows client defaults (auto-tuning normal, ECN disabled on most builds).
tweaks.proposedState: Current state reported; optionally auto-tuning level and/or ECN capability set and verified.

verify.procedure: Re-parsed `netsh int tcp show global` matches each requested value; inspection-only runs report parseOk and the parsed fields.

rollback.procedure: Only-if-ours per parameter: a field still matching the NEXTRIX-written value is set back to the captured prior value; a field the owner changed is reported diverged. Raw prior output is journaled with the entry.

originalState.method: Raw `netsh int tcp show global` text (truncated to a bounded size) plus parsed fields captured before any set.

sideEffects: A non-default auto-tuning level or ECN mode changes stack behavior in ways that are workload-dependent; no outcome is claimed.
Applies immediately (no reboot).

tweaks.name: MTU inspection & configuration
tweaks.description: Inspects and configures the per-interface, per-family MTU against a documented path-MTU symptom.
tweaks.objective: Provide a precise, reversible MTU control for the documented symptom class (black-holed large packets on VPN/PPPoE/tunnel paths).
tweaks.technicalExplanation: TROUBLESHOOTING: intended for a named symptom (some sites/services unreachable while small requests work), not for general tuning. Per interface and per address family via Get-/Set-NetIPInterface (NlMtuBytes); IPv6 is refused below the documented 1280 minimum, IPv4 below 576, and a disconnected/never-configured interface that exposes no MTU value is skipped instead of coerced to zero. The default selection is the interface carrying a default route unless an interface is named explicitly. The entry reports - but does not silently change - an inconsistency where the adapter jumbo keyword is still Disabled while the interface MTU is above 1500: an MTU larger than the path supports makes the symptom worse. PRESET-EXCLUDED and consent-gated; rollback restores the captured MTU only while the live value is still ours. Read-only inspection is available through the diagnostics entry NX07-019.
tweaks.defaultState: Interface default (commonly 1500 IPv4 / 1500 or 1280 IPv6, DHCP/RA-provided).
tweaks.proposedState: Chosen MTU on the affected interface/family, journaled and verified.

verify.procedure: Re-read of Get-NetIPInterface returns the requested NlMtuBytes for the target interface/family; a jumbo/MTU mismatch above 1500 is reported.

rollback.procedure: Only-if-ours restore of the captured MTU; interfaces that disappeared or expose no MTU are reported diverged.

originalState.method: Per-interface/per-family NlMtuBytes captured before the write (absent values recorded as unavailable, never as zero).

sideEffects: An MTU above what the path supports can drop large packets; below-path values trade payload size per packet.
Applies immediately.

tweaks.name: Network diagnostics report
tweaks.description: Read-only baseline report: adapter statistics, IP configuration, default routes, DNS servers, TCP global state and DNS cache entry count.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner a reproducible before/after snapshot without producing any performance verdict.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Collects Get-NetAdapterStatistics (bytes, unicast packets, packet errors, discarded packets), Get-NetIPConfiguration, default routes for IPv4/IPv6, Get-DnsClientServerAddress, the parsed `netsh int tcp show global` fields and a DNS cache ENTRY COUNT. DNS cache CONTENT is deliberately not exported: cached names are browsing history and would leak personal data into a shareable report. MAC addresses are masked to the vendor OUI. pathping is opt-in (-IncludePathPing with a plain hostname/IP target) and can take minutes; when enabled its output is included but no verdict is derived from it. A JSON file can be written to a caller-chosen folder; the function never writes to an implicit location. Read-only: no mutation and no journal requirement (a ReportOnly entry is journaled only when a journal directory is supplied).
tweaks.defaultState: Information only.
tweaks.proposedState: Machine-readable diagnostics object (and optional JSON file).

verify.procedure: Report carries readOnly=true, every adapter with counters, the IP/route/DNS sections, tcpGlobal.parseOk and dnsCacheEntryCount; no DNS names appear anywhere.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - read-only diagnostic.

originalState.method: Not applicable - read-only.

sideEffects: None (read-only). Optional pathping can take minutes and sends probe traffic.

tweaks.name: DNS cache management
tweaks.description: Flushes the DNS client cache for a documented stale-name symptom, with the operation and entry counts journaled.
tweaks.objective: Resolve a named stale-resolution symptom with a single documented operation and an audit record.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: TROUBLESHOOTING: calls Clear-DnsClientCache (documented) after capturing the cache entry count, and journals an operation entry (targetType dnsCacheClear) with before/after counts. Not scheduled, not automatic. The operation is honestly NOT reversible: a flushed cache repopulates on demand and there is nothing to restore - the journal records that this happened so an owner can correlate it with a symptom. Verification is the documented command result plus an entry-count check; a non-zero count immediately afterwards is reported as Partial (concurrent resolution legitimately repopulates entries) rather than as failure. This is not a performance action and makes no claim.
tweaks.defaultState: Cache holds whatever the system resolved recently.
tweaks.proposedState: Cache flushed; counts recorded; operation journaled.

verify.procedure: Clear-DnsClientCache succeeded and the entry count is 0 (Verified) or non-zero with a Partial note explaining concurrent repopulation.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable by design - a flushed cache repopulates; the journal records the operation for correlation.

originalState.method: DNS cache entry COUNT captured before the flush (content is never recorded - it is personal data).

sideEffects: Next resolutions are uncached until the cache warms again (owner-visible; no latency claim).
documentationSource: r5-winutil-sophia.md (Clear-DnsClientCache used at the end of DNS changes)

tweaks.name: Network stack reset
tweaks.description: Consent-gated last-resort reset of the Winsock catalog and TCP/IP stacks for a documented unrecoverable networking symptom, with a full pre-state report.
tweaks.objective: Offer the documented reset only as a symptom-driven last resort, with the consequences and the pre-state spelled out before anything runs.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: TROUBLESHOOTING + last resort. Requires BOTH -Approved and -AcknowledgeConsequences; the throw text lists the consequences verbatim. Before running anything it builds and journals a FULL PRE-STATE report: adapters (masked MACs), `ipconfig /all` text, per-interface DNS and MTU/DHCP state, the route table, parsed TCP global state, and the Winsock catalog entry count/sample. It then runs the three documented resets only - `netsh winsock reset`, `netsh int ip reset <log>`, `netsh int ipv6 reset <log>` - with the log files written into the journal directory. HONESTLY IRREVERSIBLE: the journal stores the pre-state and the command list, not an automatic restore, and the verify entry records Success-Irreversible with Verification RebootRequired (or Failed-Irreversible). DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: `netsh advfirewall reset` (destroys owner firewall rules), IPv6 removal/binding strip, adapter deletion, and any registry-level LSP surgery - all recorded rejected patterns in the research. A reboot is required for the reset to be fully in effect.
tweaks.defaultState: Current Winsock catalog and TCP/IP stack configuration.
tweaks.proposedState: Documented stacks reset to their default state; pre-state and reset logs preserved in the journal.

verify.procedure: Each reset command's exit code is recorded; the verify entry is Success-Irreversible with RebootRequired (or Failed-Irreversible naming the failing command). The pre-state object is retrievable from the journal.

rollback.procedure: NOT journal-reversible by design: rollback reports Skipped-Irreversible and points to the journaled pre-state (static IP/DNS/MTU values, route table, Winsock entry count) plus the reset logs for manual reconstruction.

originalState.method: Full pre-state report (adapters, ipconfig /all, DNS, MTU/DHCP, routes, TCP global, Winsock catalog count/sample) journaled before the first command.

sideEffects: Network briefly disconnects; adapters re-enumerate.
Static IP/DNS/MTU settings may be reset and are NOT re-applied automatically.
Third-party Winsock LSP entries are removed; those products may need repair.
Reboot required.
documentationSource: r3-sapphire-vain.md (Vain full-stack reset at install - narrowed here to documented resets)

tweaks.name: Per-game QoS/DSCP profile
tweaks.description: Creates one per-application QoS policy that marks a chosen game's traffic with DSCP 46 (opt-in), scoped to a single profile name.
tweaks.objective: Provide a per-game DSCP marking as an explicit opt-in, removable by name, without pretending the router honors it.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Creates ONE policy with the documented New-NetQosPolicy surface: -AppPathNameMatchCondition <full exe path>, -DSCPAction (default 46), -PolicyStore <computer name> so it persists locally, -NetworkProfile All, -Precedence. The exe must exist (full path, .exe), DSCP must be 0..63, and the policy name defaults to NEXTRIX-QoS-<exe>; an existing policy with that name is NEVER overwritten or claimed (it may be the owner's) - the function skips with PolicyExistsNotOurs. Verification re-reads the created policy and compares its application path and DSCP value. Rollback removes ONLY the exact policy this function created, and only while its fields still match the recorded ones; a policy the owner edited is reported diverged and left in place. HONEST SCOPE: DSCP is a marking, not a guarantee - it is only honored end-to-end when the router/access point and the path honor DSCP, and Windows/policy can override markings; NEXTRIX therefore makes NO latency/Jitter/prioritization claim and the entry is E0, opt-in and preset-excluded. This is the SapphireOS 'Auto DSCP & FSE' idea narrowed to the documented QoS policy surface only (no FSE/GPU-preference side effects).
tweaks.defaultState: No NEXTRIX QoS policy for the application.
tweaks.proposedState: One persistent per-application QoS policy with the chosen DSCP marking, journaled by name.

verify.procedure: Get-NetQosPolicy -Name <recorded name> -PolicyStore <computer> returns a policy whose application path and DSCP value match the requested ones; a mismatch removes the just-created policy and journals the failure.

rollback.procedure: Removes ONLY the recorded policy name while its app path and DSCP still equal the recorded values; absent policies report already-absent, edited policies report diverged and are left untouched.

originalState.method: Policy name existence check (refuses if present) plus the recorded name/store/app path/DSCP before creation.

sideEffects: Marking is effective only if network equipment honors DSCP - router/infrastructure dependent.
A stale policy persists until rolled back explicitly (journal holds the name).
documentationSource: r3-sapphire-vain.md (Auto DSCP & FSE per-game profile idea; DHCP/DSCP scope narrowed)
